translationRepairs: Emperor Gongmin Hui—Zhu Yunwen—bore the tabooed name Yunwen.
Emperor Gongmin Hui bore the tabooed name Yunwen.
The Chinese 恭閔惠皇帝諱允炆 names only the posthumous title and the tabooed given name; Zhu Yunwen is an inserted surname-plus-given not present in the source.
On guimao of the twelfth month He Fu routed and slew Dao Gan Meng, and Lucian was brought to peace.
On guimao of the twelfth month He Fu routed and slew Dao Gan Meng, and Luchuan was brought to peace.
麓川 is the toponym Luchuan, not the personal name Lucian.
On the guimao day of the twelfth month, He Fu defeated and beheaded Dao Gan Meng; Lucian was pacified.
On the guimao day of the twelfth month, He Fu defeated and beheaded Dao Gan Meng; Luchuan was pacified.
麓川 is the toponym Luchuan, not the personal name Lucian.
His younger brothers Yun Teng were enfeoffed as Prince of Wu, Yun Jie as Prince of Heng, and Yun Xi as Prince of Xu.
His younger brother Yun Teng was enfeoffed as Prince of Wu, Yun Jie as Prince of Heng, and Yun Xi as Prince of Xu.
The literal rendering makes a plural verb agree with the first brother's name alone; the Chinese lists three brothers with three fiefs.
In the sixth month Prince Min Zhu Zhen was stripped of rank and exiled to Zhangzhou.
In the sixth month Prince Min Zhu Pian was stripped of rank and exiled to Zhangzhou.
楩 is Pian, not Zhen; the given-name romanization does not match the Chinese character.
Chief steward Ge Cheng, Commander Lu Zhen, and Reader Yu Fengchen died defending the city.
Chief steward Ge Cheng, Commander Lu Zhen, and Reader Yu Fengchen died in the affair.
死之 means they died in the affair; the Chinese does not say they died defending a city.
The edict said: "The state has met misfortune; bone kin of the Zhou lineage have repeatedly plotted usurpation.
The edict said: "The state has met misfortune; close flesh-and-blood kin have repeatedly plotted usurpation.
周親 means close kin, not members of a Zhou lineage; the literal rendering invents a dynastic name.
In the fifth month, on the xinwei day, Li Jinglong rushed to Jinan.
In the fifth month, on the xinwei day, he rushed to Jinan.
The Chinese 奔濟南 has a silent subject; the idiomatic line invents the personal name Li Jinglong.
On the jiashen day, Xu Huihu, Duke of Wei, took the field to relieve Shandong.
On the jiashen day, Xu Huizu, Duke of Wei, took the field to relieve Shandong.
輝祖 is Huizu, not Huihu; the given-name romanization does not match the Chinese.
On the jiaxu day, Xu Huihu and his colleagues broke the Yan army at Qimei Mountain and killed their general Li Bin; the Yan troops wavered and talked of marching north again.
On the jiaxu day, Xu Huizu and his colleagues broke the Yan army at Qimei Mountain and killed their general Li Bin; the Yan troops wavered and talked of marching north again.
輝祖 is Huizu, not Huihu.
Just then the emperor heard a rumor that the Yan army had already withdrawn north; he recalled Xu Huihu, leaving He Fu's force stranded alone.
Just then the emperor heard a rumor that the Yan army had already withdrawn north; he recalled Xu Huizu, leaving He Fu's force stranded alone.
輝祖 is Huizu, not Huihu.
On the xinyou day, the princes were ordered to man separate sectors of the capital; Li Jinglong, Minister of War Ru Yao, and Commander Wang Zuo were sent to the Yan camp to plead the old terms again.

On the xinyou day, the princes were ordered to man separate sectors of the capital; Li Jinglong, Minister of War Ru Chang, and Commander Wang Zuo were sent to the Yan camp to plead the old terms again.
茹瑺 is Ru Chang (瑺 = Chang), not Ru Yao; the given-name romanization does not match the Chinese.

On the xinyou day, the princes were ordered to guard the capital by separate assignments; Li Jinglong together with Minister of War Ru Yao and Commander Wang Zuo were sent to the Yan army to renew the previous agreement.

茹瑺 is Ru Chang (瑺 = Chang), not Ru Yao; the given-name romanization does not match the Chinese.
